---
title: "Foundation 5A: Barcodes and persistence diagrams"
toc: true
---

Persistent homology records when each homology class first appears and how
long it remains distinguishable as the filtration grows. Its **birth** is the
first scale at which it appears. Its **death** is the scale at which it merges
into an older component or becomes trivial in homology. The usual outputs are
two views of those values.

[]{#two-views-of-the-same-intervals}

A **barcode** draws one horizontal interval for each class, from its birth
scale to its death scale. It makes lifespans and the number of classes alive
at a chosen scale easy to read. A **persistence diagram** represents the same
class by the point $(\text{birth},\text{death})$. It is more compact and is the
usual starting point for comparing or statistically analysing several
persistence outputs. Neither display contains more interval information than
the other.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .insight}
**Two views, one record.** A barcode reads like a timetable. A persistence
diagram collects the same start and finish values as coordinates; distance
above the diagonal shows lifespan.
:::

<iframe class="abc-persistence-explorer"
src="../../assets/abc-persistence-explorer.html"
title="Explore the A/B/C Rips filtration with degree-zero and degree-one barcodes and persistence diagrams"
scrolling="no"
loading="lazy"></iframe>

Move $\varepsilon$ from left to right. The Rips complex grows in the left
panel. In $H_0$, component bars end as components merge. In $H_1$, a bar begins
when a new loop class appears and ends when that class is filled. Its diagram
point remains at the corresponding birth and death coordinates.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .qualification}
**Parameter convention.** Here $\varepsilon$ is the pairwise-distance
threshold used by the software. The faint balls have radius
$\varepsilon/2$, and an edge enters when its endpoints are at most
$\varepsilon$ apart.
:::

The colours connect the same feature families across the complex, barcode and
diagram panels.
The local loops appear at the scale of the B-shaped groups. The darker point
and bar record the later, larger A-scale loop. Shorter grey intervals record
other loops created by this particular point sample and Rips construction.

Neither display shows where a representative cycle lies in the data. A long
lifespan records survival across filtration scale, not automatic scientific
importance. Its meaning still depends on the data and construction choices.

::: {.checkpoint-route}

You are ready to continue when you can follow one feature from the growing
complex to its bar and diagram point, and explain what those two displays
retain and omit.

:::
